Existing grant was multi-year and project-based, matching KABIL's institutional scale and program design.
ABF's CSR spend grew ~4.7x in four years (₹91 cr FY20-21 → ₹427 cr FY24-25).

items.justification: Environment/water (CONSERW/Jaldhara) is a real, actively-funded SBIF vertical directly supporting KABIL — but SBIF's largest bucket is Health (~40% of spend), outside KABIL's scope.

Confirmed active project in Udalguri; SBIF's own channels separately name the districts of Baksa and Udalguri in Assam.

Fits SBIF's typical ₹50L–5Cr, 1–3-year RFP band well; slight deduction because KABIL's specific grant amount/duration within that band isn't publicly confirmed.
SBIF funding grew roughly 3x in three years; share of SBI's total CSR budget routed through the Foundation grew ~50%→~60%.

Weakest-scored criterion in the exercise — only evidence is a historical/legacy link via Sir Dorabji Tata Trust from KABIL's 2013-14 founding year (cached snippet from a page that now 404s), not confirmed currently active. Cold-to-lukewarm prospect despite KABIL's website listing.
Hand-vetting revision (was 6): SDTT small grants cover only 80–90% of project cost (NGO co-finances the rest), and Tata's scale-up is explicitly going to fewer, much larger flagship projects.

Disbursements on track to roughly 3.5x from ₹575 cr (FY23-24) to ₹2,000 cr target (FY26-27); shifting from direct implementation toward grant-making — growing capacity despite the dormant relationship.
